title: Course Schedule
description:
There are `numCourses` courses numbered `0` to `numCourses - 1`. Each entry `[a, b]` in `prerequisites` means course `b` must be completed **before** course `a`.

Return `true` if it is possible to finish every course, otherwise `false`. This is the same as asking whether the prerequisite graph contains a cycle.
constraints: prerequisites[i].length == 2 and all pairs are distinct
hints: Model courses as nodes and prerequisites as directed edges. When is finishing everything impossible?
Impossible exactly when the directed graph has a cycle. Think of repeatedly taking courses that have no remaining prerequisites.
Kahn's algorithm: count incoming edges, queue the zero-in-degree courses, remove them and decrement their dependants. If the number processed equals numCourses there was no cycle.
starterCode:
class Solution:
    def canFinish(self, numCourses: int, prerequisites: List[List[int]]) -> bool:

args.$py: [[j,i] for i in range(100) for j in range(i+1,i+51) if j<2000][:5000]

solution.explanation: Build adjacency lists from prerequisite to dependent course and count each course's in-degree. Start a queue with all courses having in-degree zero and repeatedly pop one, decrementing the in-degree of its dependants and enqueueing any that reach zero. If every course gets processed the graph is acyclic and the answer is true; leftover courses mean a cycle. Time and space are O(V + E).
